protocol.caveat: The 19 restored models carry single-draw serial timings from the pre-contention run; these GART 2.0 / LGBM_V4 values are medians of 11 draws taken 2026-08-11. The repeat count is NOT the source of the difference: GART 2.0 median-of-11 sits within 0.97-1.05x of its own first cold draw. The difference is between RUNS -- LGBM_V3 re-measured today on the same instances runs at a median 0.70x of its restored value (0.92x for n>10000, i.e. the gap closes as real work dominates fixed overhead). Consequence: absolute time cells in tab:tsplib_by_size are comparable within a model but carry a ~1.5x between-run offset when compared ACROSS the restored and re-measured models, most of it on small n. The GART 2.0 vs LGBM_V3 ratios in gart2_over_lgbmv3_serial_ratio are free of this offset because both were measured in the same process.

cache_audit.why: TSP_V3_LGBM_Estimator memoises features on hash(coords.tobytes()), which collapses repeats into cache hits. Every estimator timed here was audited for the same pattern before its repeats were trusted.
cache_audit.static: each of the five holds only 1-3 scalar attributes (region_mode, enforce_n_range, variant, enforce_domain); no dict, list or set on the object grows across calls, and no new attribute appears. classical_region_estimators.py contains no lru_cache, no memo dict and no tobytes key.
cache_audit.dynamic_uncleared_repeats: 5 back-to-back calls with NO cache clearing, ratios call_k/call_0: 0.91-1.25 on d18512 (n=18,512) and 0.60-1.19 on pr152 (n=152). A memoised estimator returns ratios near 0.01.
cache_audit.verdict: no result caching in any of the five; the 11 repeats measure 11 full computations.
